tips.title: Lead with scale and stakes, not job titles
tips.detail: "Managed a 16-person team executing a 9-month phased operation with zero schedule slippage" reads better to a construction hiring manager than a military rank or MOS title alone.

tips.title: Quantify everything you can
tips.detail: Team sizes, budgets/equipment values managed, timelines, number of coordinated elements — numbers translate across industries even when job titles don't.

tips.title: Use construction-adjacent verbs
tips.detail: Coordinated, inspected, documented, verified, scheduled, escalated, mitigated — these mirror the language of a job description for a Field Engineer.

tips.title: Translate, don't just list
tips.detail: Instead of listing a military project name alone, add a one-line "translation" clause showing the civilian equivalent skill.

tips.title: Keep a civilian-readable summary at the top
tips.detail: A 2-3 sentence summary translating your background before the detailed experience section helps a non-military reader immediately understand your fit.
